passages.t: ‘He heals the brokenhearted’ and ‘calls the stars by name’
passages.happening:
Psalm 147 opens with joy. “Hallelujah! How good it is to sing praises to our God, how pleasant and lovely to praise Him!” (verse 1).

“The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers the exiles of Israel” (verse 2). “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds” (verse 3). And in the next breath: “He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name” (verse 4). “Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit” (verse 5).

He lifts the humble and throws down the wicked (verse 6). He brings the clouds and the rain and makes grass grow on the hills (verse 8). “He provides food for the animals, and for the young ravens when they call” (verse 9).

What does he delight in? Not in the strength of horses or the speed of runners (verse 10). “The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion” (verse 11).
passages.hearers:
‘He gathers the exiles’ and ‘builds up Jerusalem’ point to the time after the exile, when the city was being rebuilt. Many scholars date this psalm to then. When the rebuilt walls were finished, the Levites were brought in “to celebrate the joyous dedication with thanksgiving and singing” (Nehemiah 12:27).

Put verses 3 and 4 side by side. The God who counts and names every star is the same God who bends down to bandage a broken heart. Greatness and tenderness belong together in him.

Ravens were unclean birds in Israel's law (Leviticus 11:15). Even their young, calling out for food, are fed by God.

The war horse was the strongest weapon of the ancient world. God is not impressed by it. He takes pleasure in people who trust his love.

In the Greek Old Testament, this psalm is divided into two psalms, as the book page explains in its part on numbering.
passages.later:
Isaiah said of the stars, “He calls each one by name” (Isaiah 40:26), and of God's servant, “He has sent Me to bind up the brokenhearted” (Isaiah 61:1).

Jesus said, “Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!” (Luke 12:24).
passages.asks:
Is your heart broken? Verse 3 is for you. The God who named the stars binds up wounds. He is not too big to notice you.

And what are you relying on: strength, speed, resources? Verse 11 says God is pleased with those who hope in his loving devotion. That is something anyone can do.

passages.t: ‘He spreads the snow like wool’, and His word to Jacob
passages.happening:
A new call goes out. “Exalt the LORD, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion!” (verse 12). God has made the city's gates strong and blessed its children (verse 13). “He makes peace at your borders; He fills you with the finest wheat” (verse 14).

Then the psalm looks at the weather. “He sends forth His command to the earth; His word runs swiftly” (verse 15). “He spreads the snow like wool; He scatters the frost like ashes” (verse 16). His hail falls like pebbles, and no one can stand the cold (verse 17). Then “He sends forth His word and melts them” (verse 18), and the waters flow again.

The same word that rules the snow is spoken to God's people. “He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel” (verse 19). “He has done this for no other nation; they do not know His judgments. Hallelujah!” (verse 20).
passages.hearers:
A first hearer would picture white wool on the ground, frost scattered like grey ash, and then the thaw.

Notice the word ‘word’. In verses 15 and 18 God's word commands the weather and the snow obeys. In verse 19 that same word is given to Israel as teaching. The God who rules the world has spoken to his people. That is the gift verse 20 celebrates.

Verse 20 is not boasting. It is wonder. Israel had been given God's teaching, not because it was great, but because God chose to give it.
passages.later:
Paul says of the Jewish people that “they have been entrusted with the very words of God” (Romans 3:2).

John's Gospel begins with God's Word: “In the beginning was the Word” (John 1:1), and says that this Word “became flesh and made His dwelling among us” (John 1:14).
passages.asks:
The God of snow and thaw is the God who speaks to you in Scripture. Do you hear his word as the gift verse 20 says it is?

Winter does not last. The same word that sends the frost sends the thaw. If you are in a cold season now, Psalm 147 says that God's word still runs swiftly, and the waters will flow.
